requirement_text.REQ-064: Execute Decision 0006's D2: drop tenant_id from ten schema-isolated business tables. Full acceptance criteria: see handoffs/WF02-REQ064-20260818/step-03-test-designer.json's requirement_text.

task.description:
TEST-DESIGNER's own run took several dispatches to complete due to unrelated infrastructure interruptions (a nested background process hit a transient API error) -- the work itself, once it finished, was independently re-verified: ORCH ran the full suite twice directly (775/775 both times) and TEST-DESIGNER's own final report separately confirms 775/775 across two of its own runs, with one flaky failure in test/letflow/identity_migration_test.exs's :auto-mode DropLegacyPublicIdentityTables guard test isolated and attributed to pre-existing connection-pool-timing flakiness (REQ-063-era code, untouched by this requirement), not a REQ-064 regression. Confirm this attribution yourself -- read that specific test, check whether this diff touched anything it depends on (it shouldn't have, per the design's own scope boundary), and if you also hit this flake, re-run just that file in isolation 3-4 times to confirm it's genuinely intermittent and not deterministic under some condition this diff introduced.

Read test/specs/REQ-064.md and the actual test source directly -- do not read TEST-DESIGNER's handoff result.summary as a substitute.

TEST-DESIGNER found and fixed a genuine production bug beyond pure test work: lib/letflow/identity_migration.ex's copy_groups/2, copy_users/2, copy_tenant_roles/2 used fragment("? = ?", g.tenant_id, ^tenant_id) which relied on the now-removed Group/User Ecto field declaration for UUID type inference -- once that field was dropped, Postgrex received a raw UUID string instead of the 16-byte binary form, causing a real DBConnection.EncodeError. Fixed with explicit type(^tenant_id, Ecto.UUID) casts. Verify this fix is correct and complete: read all three call sites directly, confirm the type/2 cast is present and correctly typed, and confirm this was a genuine pre-existing-but-latent bug this same PR's own column drop exposed (not something the fix itself introduces or masks).

Several tests were restructured (not just patched) because their entire purpose was proving something about the now-removed tenant_id field -- event_store_test.exs's AC6 block, promotion_review_store_test.exs's prefix-derivation block, store_test.exs's AC9 block, engine/schemas_test.exs's moduledoc-content test. For each, confirm the restructured version still proves the SAME underlying acceptance-criterion claim (typically via schema-prefix reachability instead of a direct field read), not a weaker or different claim.

Standard procedure: for each REQ-064 acceptance criterion, verify at least one runnable test targets it, no TODO-implement-test deferrals, tests self-sufficient and don't depend on execution order, no hardcoded secrets/connection strings, per-test unique fixture data.
acceptance_criteria: Every REQ-064 acceptance criterion has at least one runnable test, verified against actual test source
The identity_migration_test.exs flake independently confirmed pre-existing/unrelated, not a REQ-064 regression
identity_migration.ex's type(^tenant_id, Ecto.UUID) fix verified correct at all three call sites

Each restructured test (event_store_test.exs, promotion_review_store_test.exs, store_test.exs, engine/schemas_test.exs) confirmed to still prove its original acceptance-criterion claim, not a weaker one
Test fixtures use per-test unique data, no shared hardcoded tenant/schema names

result.summary:
Items 1 and 2 of this gate independently confirmed clean: (1) test/letflow/identity_migration_test.exs is entirely absent from `git diff main...HEAD --stat` -- only lib/letflow/identity_migration.ex (the production module it exercises) is touched. Ran the file in isolation 4x (`mix test test/letflow/identity_migration_test.exs`), 7/7 passed every time -- the reported flake is confirmed pre-existing/unrelated, not a REQ-064 regression. (2) All three call sites in identity_migration.ex (copy_groups/2 line 127, copy_users/2 line 132, copy_tenant_roles/2 line 159) read directly: each now uses `fragment("? = ?", g.tenant_id, type(^tenant_id, Ecto.UUID))` / `u.tenant_id` -- the Ecto.UUID cast is present and correctly typed at all three sites, and identity_migration_test.exs's own passing runs exercise copy_tenant/2 (which calls all three) against real Postgres, confirming the fix works at runtime, not just compiles.

Item 3 FAILS. event_store_test.exs's, promotion_review_store_test.exs's, and store_test.exs's restructures were read against their diffs and are sound -- each replaces a direct tenant_id field-equality assertion with a schema-prefix reachability check that is an equal-or-stronger proof of the same underlying claim (own-schema reachability plus explicit cross-schema unreachability against a second, independently provisioned tenant). engine/schemas_test.exs's moduledoc-text assertion was verified directly against lib/letflow/engine/task.ex lines 39/45 -- the asserted strings ('No `tenant_id` column (Decision 0006 D2)', 'Do not re-add a `tenant_id` field to this schema') are genuinely present.

But test/specs/REQ-064.md's own traceability table (row for 'TenantProvisioning.tenant_id_for_schema_name/1 itself still exists and is tested', line 217) makes a specific, checkable claim that is factually false: it says event_store_test.exs's restructured AC6 test 'already asserts `{:ok, expected_tenant_id} = TenantProvisioning.tenant_id_for_schema_name(schema_name)` as a genuine round-trip check' and that this satisfies the acceptance criterion with 'no new test needed... confirmed by direct inspection this session, not assumed.' Reading the actual diff for event_store_test.exs shows that exact assertion (`assert {:ok, expected_tenant_id} = TenantProvisioning.tenant_id_for_schema_name(schema_name)` plus `assert expected_tenant_id == tenant_id`) was REMOVED as part of the restructure, not kept -- `grep -n "tenant_id_for_schema_name" test/letflow/event_store_test.exs` returns zero hits post-diff. This is not just a stale traceability note: grepping the entire test/ tree for `tenant_id_for_schema_name` finds only three other hits (test/letflow/definitions_test.exs:212, a moduledoc-string assertion `doc =~ "tenant_id_for_schema_name"` that never calls the function; test/letflow/definitions/promotion_review_store_test.exs:277 and test/letflow/definitions/rollback_test.exs:126, both comments, no calls). The dedicated test/letflow/tenant_provisioning_test.exs file tests schema_name_for_tenant/1 directly but has zero references to tenant_id_for_schema_name/1. So this pure function (lib/letflow/tenant_provisioning.ex lines 100-115: a real round-trip transform with its own {:ok, uuid} / {:error, :invalid_schema_name} contract) is exercised only as an opaque pass-through inside various `with` chains across the suite (definitions.ex/event_store.ex call sites) -- no test anywhere asserts on its actual input/output contract (correct round-trip, or the malformed-input error path) after this diff. REQ-064's own acceptance criteria explicitly require 'TenantProvisioning.tenant_id_for_schema_name/1 itself still exists and is still tested' -- this is not satisfied, and the spec's claim that it is was not independently re-verified before being written down.

Did not evaluate item 4's remaining sub-checks exhaustively (skip-tag/TODO sweep across changed test files came back clean, no hardcoded secrets observed) since item 3's failure is already sufficient grounds for FAIL per this gate's 'FAIL immediately on any check failure' rule -- no partial credit.

issues.description: test/specs/REQ-064.md line 217's traceability-table claim that event_store_test.exs's restructured AC6 test still asserts `{:ok, expected_tenant_id} = TenantProvisioning.tenant_id_for_schema_name(schema_name)` is false -- git diff shows that exact line was deleted by the restructure, not kept. Verify with: git diff main...HEAD -- test/letflow/event_store_test.exs (search the 'tenant_id (AC6)' describe block) and grep -n tenant_id_for_schema_name test/letflow/event_store_test.exs (zero hits).

Resulting real gap: TenantProvisioning.tenant_id_for_schema_name/1 (lib/letflow/tenant_provisioning.ex:102-115, the pure schema-name-to-tenant-UUID reverse-derivation function with its own {:ok, uuid}/{:error, :invalid_schema_name} contract) has no test anywhere in the suite that calls it directly or asserts on its return value. grep -rn tenant_id_for_schema_name test/ finds only: definitions_test.exs:212 (a moduledoc doc-string substring assertion, never invokes the function), promotion_review_store_test.exs:277 and rollback_test.exs:126 (comments only), and every call inside definitions.ex/event_store.ex's own `with` chains is exercised only as an opaque pass-through gate (tests assert on the overall function's success/failure, never on tenant_id_for_schema_name/1's own round-trip correctness or its :invalid_schema_name error path specifically). REQ-064's acceptance criteria explicitly require this function be 'still tested' -- it is not, post-restructure. Needs either: restore a direct round-trip assertion (the exact assertion event_store_test.exs used to have, or an equivalent in tenant_provisioning_test.exs which already tests schema_name_for_tenant/1 the same way), or add one to tenant_provisioning_test.exs directly (covering both the success round-trip and the :invalid_schema_name error path), and correct test/specs/REQ-064.md's traceability table to match whichever fix is chosen.
